title: You say you have faith…
paragraphs:
You say you have faith…
…but why does it disappear the moment life gets hard?
Because this might expose something you’ve been hiding—even from yourself.

You sing the songs.
You post the verses.
You say “God is good” with a steady voice.

You’re anxious.
Controlling.
Afraid of losing everything.
And here’s the question we avoid:
Is that faith… or is that fear dressed like faith?

Because this isn’t about religion.
This is about truth.
…but you still need to see the outcome first.
…but only when the situation feels safe.
…but you keep your backup plans hidden in your pocket.
And control feels safe—until it collapses.

Until the diagnosis comes.
Until the relationship breaks.
Until the money runs out.
Until the doors slam shut.
The version of “faith” we built starts shaking.
We don’t struggle to believe in God’s existence.
We struggle to trust His character.
Because real faith will take you somewhere uncomfortable.
Somewhere where your strength is not enough.
God gave him a promise that sounded impossible.

But time kept moving.
Years passed.
His body weakened.
Sarah’s womb stayed closed.
“Against all hope, Abraham in hope believed…” — Romans 4:18
Meaning everything visible said, “This won’t happen.”
But Abraham chose to trust anyway.
Yes—even the father of faith had moments of failure.

Moments where he stepped outside of trust
and into human effort.
Trying to force what only God can fulfill.
Trying to control what only God can carry.
Trying to fix what only God can redeem.
The kind we don’t post about.

“You don’t really trust God.”
“You’re not as faithful as you think.”
“You’re a fraud.”
That’s where you are right now.
Let me take you to another moment.
Peter stepped out of the boat.
Walking toward Jesus on the water.

The wind.
The waves.
The chaos.
Jesus didn’t wait for Peter to fix himself.
“O you of little faith, why did you doubt?” — Matthew 14:31

Jesus didn’t say,
“Why did you fail, Peter?”
Because the issue wasn’t Peter’s weakness.
It was where his eyes shifted.

And our eyes move from Christ…
to chaos.
Faith is not what saves you.
“For by grace you have been saved through faith. And this is not your own doing; it is the gift of God.”
It’s the empty hand that receives the gift.
You don’t earn salvation by having strong faith.
You receive salvation by trusting a strong Savior.
Because here’s the truth we don’t say enough:
“But God shows his love for us in that while we were still sinners, Christ died for us.”
Not when you had perfect faith.
Not when you had everything together.
Not when you were spiritually strong.
While you were still a sinner.
Your weakness didn’t scare Him away.
And paid for it—fully—on the cross.
Faith is not about proving something to God.
It’s about surrendering to what Jesus already finished.
You don’t need to fake strength.
You don’t need to hide your fear.
You don’t need to perform spirituality.

Come with weak faith.
Come with trembling hands.
Come with questions and scars.
Because salvation is not built on your ability to hold on to God.
It’s built on God’s ability to hold on to you.
“I give them eternal life, and they will never perish, and no one will snatch them out of my hand.”
“God, I don’t understand this… but I trust You.”
It’s choosing obedience when it’s inconvenient.
It’s surrendering control when everything in you wants to grab it back.
It’s fixing your eyes on Jesus—
even when the storm is screaming louder.
“Now faith is the assurance of things hoped for, the conviction of things not seen.”
God is exposing something in you.
Because fake faith will exhaust you.
Lay down the version of faith you’ve been performing.
Jesus is not asking you for perfection.
Let that be your starting point.
